text:
Jake Oettinger stopped 33 shots in a 1-0 win over Pittsburgh on Nov. 22, his league-best fifth shutout, as the Toronto Star put it. By our numbers he's the most valuable goalie in the league so far: first among 79 in wins added through saves, 12.36 goals saved above expected (goals he stopped beyond what an average goalie would on those shots), a .909 save percentage and a 13-4-1 record in 18 starts.

The separation is on medium-danger shots, .914 against .861 for the league; on high danger he's about average, .686 against .684. Rebound control is excellent: 8.4% of his saves lead to another shot within three seconds (league 10.7%). It hasn't been flawless, he played only 41 minutes in Winnipeg on Nov. 12, but he has answered with strong nights since. Jesse Granger of The Athletic singled out a stop on Brett Howden against Vegas, "Incredible read by Jake Oettinger to rob Brett Howden on the backdoor of a 2-on-1 with Eichel." Last season was much more ordinary by our count, 2.2 goals saved above expected, which is what makes this run stand out.
headline: Jake Oettinger is saving Dallas more than anyone
